context_candidates.text: Any specific region is considered covered by data in a given year if the economies with at least one survey within a three-year window on either side of the year account for at least 50 percent of the region’s population. Because of a lack of data, neither the Middle East and North Africa nor Sub-Saharan Africa were included among the post-2020 data in Poverty, Prosperity, and Planet Report 2024 (World Bank 2024a). Since then, more recent data have become available for a number of populous economies, greatly increasing the regional and global coverage in the post-COVID years. The updates include data on Ethiopia (2021) and Nigeria (2022/23), which results in coverage for Sub-Saharan Africa up to 2024, as well as new data for the Arab Republic of Egypt (2021/22), India (2022/23, 2023/24), and Pakistan (2024/25).

context_candidates.text: Poverty varies sharply across these groups, even within economies at similar income levels (World Bank 2018). Children under age 18 face the highest rates of extreme poverty of any age-group. Individuals with no formal education face the highest rates of any educational group. Across these groups, rates of extreme poverty vary substantially, though all groups experienced declining poverty rates between 2013 and 2024. Age represents a stark divide.

Across these groups, rates of extreme poverty vary substantially, though all groups experienced declining poverty rates between 2013 and 2024. Age represents a stark divide.
